findings: Assign application and verification scaffolding to a delivery slice, with its required paths and dependencies. The mounted src/ contains only .gitkeep, package.json defines no application build, typecheck, unit or browser commands, and CI runs only the documentation/baseline verify chain. None of the issue-4 through issue-14 bounded task lists owns the browser entrypoint, test configuration or command/CI wiring needed to deliver and check the planned application.

Reconcile the bounded paths with the shared command architecture before implementation. Issue-4 owns domain.ts but covers only song/section commands; issue-6 introduces repertoire/membership mutations with only Library.tsx and an end-to-end test in scope, and later mutation slices similarly omit shared command/domain paths. Assign ownership and permitted paths for the pure operations and serialized, mode-guarded application boundary, including direct-command refusal tests, so later slices can enforce invariants without moving domain logic into UI components or exceeding their bounds.

Fix issue-10's dependency on note editing: its SB-OFFLINE acceptance requires editing a note through the application while disconnected, but annotations are introduced by issue-11 and issue-10 depends only on issue-9. Add issue-11 as a prerequisite or move core annotation editing into an earlier slice, and update the dependency records so issue-10 can independently complete its declared browser journey.

Complete the backup delivery and verification plan in issue-12/issue-14. Issue-12 bounds implementation to backup.ts and a unit-test file, while issue-14's browser scenarios cover only rejected imports; no slice explicitly owns the download, file-selection and replacement-confirmation UI or a successful browser round trip. Assign those paths and plan download-to-file, import into a different populated library, confirmation/cancellation and reload checks that compare all identities, associations and content, extending coverage to attachment bytes when issue-13 is delivered.

Add a concrete service-worker update journey to issue-10's verification plan. Its only declared scenario is SB-OFFLINE, but docs/architecture/08-crosscutting-concepts promises explicit user-controlled activation and docs/profiles/pwa-capability/testing.md requires a clean-profile, two-revision browser check. Plan a production-build test that leaves the new worker waiting during performance consultation, activates it only on user action, and verifies that acknowledged local content survives the update and a subsequent offline reload.
